passages.ctx: From the Sermon on the Mount.
passages.en: Blessed are the merciful, because they themselves will be shown mercy.

passages.ctx: Jesus sends out the twelve apostles.
passages.en: The one welcoming you welcomes me, and the one welcoming me welcomes the one who sent me.

passages.ctx: Jesus answers those who say he drives out demons by Beelzebul.
passages.en: The one who is not with me is against me, and the one who does not gather with me scatters.

passages.ctx: Jesus begins to explain the parable of the sower to his disciples.
passages.en: You, then, listen to the parable of the sower.

passages.ctx: In the parable, a vineyard owner answers a worker who grumbles about his pay.
passages.en: But he, answering one of them, said, ‘Friend, I am not wronging you. Was it not for a denarius that you agreed with me?’

passages.ctx: In the parable of the wedding feast, a guest has no wedding garment.
passages.en: Then the king said to the servants, ‘Tie his feet and hands, and throw him out into the darkness outside. There will be the weeping and the grinding of teeth.’

passages.ctx: Jesus speaks against the scribes and Pharisees.
passages.en: But woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites, because you lock the kingdom of the heavens in front of people; for you are not going in, nor do you let those who are going in enter.

passages.ctx: Jesus teaches in the synagogue at Capernaum.
passages.en: And they were astounded at his teaching, for he was teaching them like someone who has authority, and not like the scribes.

passages.ctx: Jesus leaves the synagogue at Capernaum with his first disciples.
passages.en: And at once, coming out of the synagogue, they went into the house of Simon and Andrew with James and John.

passages.ctx: Jesus is teaching in a crowded house in Capernaum.
passages.en: And they come, bringing a paralysed man to him, carried by four.

passages.ctx: The disciples have asked Jesus about the parable of the sower.
passages.en: And he says to them, ‘You do not know this parable? And how will you come to know all the parables?’

passages.ctx: The local people have seen Jesus heal a man possessed by demons.
passages.en: And they began to plead with him to go away from their district.

passages.ctx: A woman who had bled for twelve years touches Jesus’ cloak.
passages.en: And at once the source of her bleeding dried up, and she knew in her body that she had been healed of the affliction.
And at once Jesus, recognizing within himself the power that had gone out from him, turning around in the crowd, kept saying, “Who touched my clothes?”

passages.ctx: Jesus has sent his disciples across the lake and stayed behind to pray.
passages.en: And as evening fell, the boat was in the middle of the sea, and he himself was alone on land.

passages.ctx: Jesus speaks about what makes a person unclean.
passages.en: And calling the crowd to him again, he was saying to them, “Hear me, every one of you, and understand.”

passages.ctx: A hungry crowd has followed Jesus into a deserted place.
passages.en: And he was asking them, “How many loaves do you have?” And they said, “Seven.”

passages.ctx: Jesus has just fed four thousand people.
passages.en: And at once, boarding the boat with his disciples, he went into the regions of Dalmanutha.

passages.ctx: Jesus ends a parable about tenants who killed the owner’s son.
passages.en: Have you not even read this scripture: ‘A stone which the builders rejected, this one became the head of the corner; from the Lord this came about, and it is wonderful in our eyes’?

passages.ctx: Jesus tells his disciples about the troubles to come.
passages.en: And to all the nations the good news must first be proclaimed.
And Judas Iscariot, the one from the twelve, went away to the chief priests so that he might hand him over to them.

passages.ctx: At the Last Supper.
passages.en: And taking a cup and giving thanks, he gave it to them, and all of them drank from it.

passages.ctx: After the supper, Jesus goes out with his disciples.
passages.en: And they come to a piece of ground whose name is Gethsemane, and he says to his disciples, “Sit here until I have prayed.”

passages.ctx: In Gethsemane, Jesus takes three disciples aside.
passages.en: And he takes along Peter and James and John with him, and he began to be utterly dismayed and in anguish, and he says to them, “My soul is deeply grieved, all the way to death. Stay here and keep awake.”

passages.ctx: In Gethsemane, Jesus wakes his sleeping disciples.
passages.en: Get up, let us go. Look, the one handing me over has come near.

passages.ctx: Jesus stands silent before Pilate.
passages.en: But Jesus no longer answered anything, so that Pilate marvelled.

passages.ctx: Mark explains a custom of Pilate’s at the Passover festival.
passages.en: Now at each festival he would release one prisoner to them, the one they requested.
But the chief priests roused the crowd, so that he would instead release Barabbas to them.
But Pilate kept saying to them, “What wrong, then, has he done?” Yet they shouted all the louder, “Crucify him!”
Now it was the third hour, and they crucified him.
And Jesus, letting out a loud cry, breathed his last.

passages.ctx: Three women come to the tomb of Jesus at sunrise.
passages.en: And going into the tomb, they saw a young man seated on the right, wrapped in a white robe, and they were struck with amazement.

passages.ctx: After his resurrection, Jesus appears to the eleven disciples.
passages.en: Later, as they were reclining at table, he was revealed to the eleven, and he reproached their unbelief and hardness of heart, because they did not believe those who had seen him raised.

passages.ctx: Mary answers the angel Gabriel.
passages.en: Then Mary said, “Here is the servant of the Lord. May it happen to me in keeping with your word.” And the angel went away from her.

passages.ctx: Elizabeth greets Mary, who has come to visit her.
passages.en: And how does this happen to me, that my Lord’s mother would come to me?

passages.ctx: Mary praises God in her song.
passages.en: He worked might with his arm; he scattered the arrogant in the thinking of their heart. He pulled rulers down from thrones and raised up the lowly; those who hunger he filled with good things, and those who are rich he sent off empty.

passages.ctx: Shepherds near Bethlehem on the night Jesus is born.
passages.en: And shepherds were in the same region, staying out in the fields and keeping the watches of the night over their flock.

passages.ctx: Jesus as a boy in Nazareth.
passages.en: And the child kept growing and getting stronger, being filled with wisdom, and God’s grace was on him.
And he was teaching in their synagogues, praised by everyone.

passages.ctx: Jesus has just healed a man with leprosy.
passages.en: And he instructed him to tell no one, “Instead, go away and show yourself to the priest, and bring an offering for your cleansing just as Moses directed, as a witness to them.”

passages.ctx: Jesus, shortly before he chooses the twelve apostles.
passages.en: Now during these days it happened that he went out to the mountain to pray, and he was spending the whole night in prayer to God.
For each tree is recognized by its own fruit. For people do not collect figs from thorn plants, nor do they harvest grapes from a bramble.

passages.ctx: A Roman centurion’s valued slave is sick and close to death.
passages.en: Hearing about Jesus, he sent elders of the Jews to him, asking him to come and rescue his slave.

passages.ctx: At Nain, Jesus meets the funeral of a widow’s only son.
passages.en: And approaching, he touched the bier; the men carrying it came to a stop, and he said, “Young man, I tell you, get up!”

passages.ctx: From the parable of the sower.
passages.en: And another fell in the midst of the thorns, and the thorns, growing up with it, choked it.

passages.ctx: Jesus explains the parable of the sower.
passages.en: Now no one, having lit a lamp, covers it with a jar or puts it under a bed, but he puts it on a lampstand, so that those coming in may see the light.

passages.ctx: Jesus has said that the daughter of Jairus is not dead but asleep.
passages.en: And they were laughing at him, knowing that she had died.

passages.ctx: Jesus has sent out the twelve.
passages.en: And setting out, they went from village to village, announcing the good news and healing everywhere.
For just as Jonah became a sign for the Ninevites, so also will the Son of Man be for this generation.

passages.ctx: Jesus speaks to the experts in the law.
passages.en: Woe to you, because you build the tombs of the prophets, but your fathers killed them.

passages.ctx: Jesus speaks of a debtor taken before a judge.
passages.en: I tell you, you will never get out of there until you have paid even the last small coin.
Now some were present at that very time, reporting to him about the Galileans whose blood Pilate had mixed with their sacrifices.
No, I tell you. But unless you repent, you will all perish in the same way.

passages.ctx: Jesus tells what the kingdom of God is like.
passages.en: It is like yeast, which a woman took and hid in three measures of flour until the whole was leavened.

passages.ctx: Jesus is on his long journey.
passages.en: And he was traveling through cities and villages, teaching and making his way to Jerusalem.

passages.ctx: In the parable, invited guests make excuses for missing a great dinner.
passages.en: And another said, ‘I married a wife, and for this reason I am not able to come.’

passages.ctx: Jesus ends the parable of the lost sheep.
passages.en: I tell you that in the same way there will be joy in heaven over one sinner who repents, more than over ninety-nine righteous people who have no need of repentance.

passages.ctx: Jesus has just taught about serving God or money.
passages.en: Now the Pharisees, being fond of money, were listening to all these things, and they were sneering at him.
And the apostles said to the Lord, ‘Grant us more faith.’
And a certain ruler questioned him, saying, ‘Good teacher, by doing what will I inherit eternal life?’

passages.ctx: A blind man by the road near Jericho hears that Jesus is passing.
passages.en: And he shouted, saying, “Jesus, Son of David, have mercy on me!”

passages.ctx: Jesus has told Zacchaeus to come down from the tree.
passages.en: And hurrying, he came down and welcomed him with joy.

passages.ctx: Jesus speaks at the house of Zacchaeus.
passages.en: And Jesus said to him, “Today salvation has come about for this house, because he too is a son of Abraham. For the Son of Man came to search for and save what has been lost.”

passages.ctx: In the parable, the servants report to their master.
passages.en: And the second one came, saying, “Your mina, master, has produced five minas.”

passages.ctx: In the parable, the owner sends a third servant.
passages.en: And he went on to send a third; but this one too they wounded and threw out.
And going out, he went, according to his custom, to the Mount of Olives; and the disciples also followed him.

passages.ctx: The council has just heard Jesus speak.
passages.en: But they said, “What further need of testimony do we have? For we ourselves heard it from his mouth.”

passages.ctx: One of the criminals crucified with Jesus rebukes the other.
passages.en: And we, for our part, are here justly, for we are getting back things worthy of what we did; but this man did nothing wrong.

passages.ctx: The risen Jesus suddenly stands among his disciples.
passages.en: But startled and becoming terrified, they thought they were seeing a spirit.

passages.ctx: John speaks of the Word.
passages.en: This one was in the beginning with God.

passages.ctx: The Gospel writer speaks of John the Baptist.
passages.en: That man was not the light, but came so that he might testify about the light.
There was the true light, which illumines every human being coming into the world.

passages.ctx: John the Baptist answers those sent to question him.
passages.en: He declared, “I am a voice of someone shouting in the desert: ‘Straighten the way of the Lord,’ just as Isaiah the prophet said.”

passages.ctx: Jesus has just met Simon Peter.
passages.en: On the next day he wanted to go out into Galilee, and he finds Philip, and Jesus says to him, “Follow me.”

passages.ctx: At a wedding in Cana, the wine has run out.
passages.en: Jesus says to them, “Fill the jars with water.” And they filled them right up to the top.

passages.ctx: In the temple, the Jews ask Jesus for a sign.
passages.en: Jesus answered and said to them, “Tear down this temple, and in three days I will raise it.”

passages.ctx: Jesus is leaving Judea for Galilee.
passages.en: Now it was necessary for him to pass through Samaria.

passages.ctx: Jesus speaks with a Samaritan woman at a well.
passages.en: Jesus says to her, “Believe me, woman, that an hour is coming when you will worship the Father neither on this mountain nor in Jerusalem.”

passages.ctx: Jesus has told the disciples he has food they know nothing of.
passages.en: So the disciples were saying to each other, “Surely no one brought him anything to eat?”

passages.ctx: At the pool, Jesus speaks to a man ill for thirty-eight years.
passages.en: Jesus says to him, “Rise, lift up your mat, and walk about.”

passages.ctx: Jesus has healed a man on the Sabbath.
passages.en: And because of this the Jews were hounding Jesus, since he was doing these things on a Sabbath.

passages.ctx: Jesus has asked Philip where to buy bread for the crowd.
passages.en: Now he was saying this to put him to the test, for he himself knew what he was about to do.

passages.ctx: Jesus has come to Jerusalem for the Festival of Booths.
passages.en: Now, with the feast already half over, Jesus went up into the temple and was teaching.

passages.ctx: Jesus answers those who accuse him.
passages.en: But I am not seeking my own glory; there is one who seeks it and who judges.
Amen, amen, I tell you, if someone keeps my word, he will never look on death, to the end of time.

passages.ctx: Neighbours question the man who was born blind.
passages.en: And they said to him, “Where is that man?” He says, “I do not know.”

passages.ctx: Some Pharisees ask Jesus whether they too are blind.
passages.en: Jesus said to them, “If you were blind, you would not have sin; but now you say, ‘We see.’ Your sin remains.”

passages.ctx: Some say Jesus has a demon, but others disagree.
passages.en: Others were saying, “These words are not those of a demon-possessed man. Surely a demon cannot open the eyes of the blind?”

passages.ctx: Martha speaks with Jesus after the death of her brother Lazarus.
passages.en: Martha says to him, “I know that he will rise at the resurrection, on the final day.”

passages.ctx: At the Last Supper, Jesus speaks to his disciples.
passages.en: Little children, I am still with you for a little while. You will look for me, and just as I said to the Jews, ‘Where I am going, you cannot come,’ now I say to you as well.
I am giving you a new command, that you love one another: just as I loved you, that you too love one another.

passages.ctx: At the Last Supper, Jesus speaks to his disciples.
passages.en: I leave you peace; I give you my peace. I do not give to you in the way the world gives. Let your heart not be troubled, nor let it lose courage.

passages.ctx: Jesus tells his disciples that he is going away.
passages.en: And now I have told you before it occurs, so that whenever it occurs, you may believe.

passages.ctx: Peter is asked a third time whether he is a disciple.
passages.en: So Peter denied it once more, and right away a rooster crowed.

passages.ctx: The chief priests ask Pilate to change the sign on the cross.
passages.en: Pilate replied, “What I have written, I have written.”

passages.ctx: Peter is travelling among the believers.
passages.en: Now it came about that Peter, while passing through every place, also came down to the saints living in Lydda.

passages.ctx: Paul, preaching in a synagogue, has just spoken of King David.
passages.en: From this man’s seed God, as promised, brought Israel a Saviour, Jesus, after John had first proclaimed, ahead of his coming, a baptism of repentance to all the people of Israel.

passages.ctx: Paul meets disciples in Ephesus who knew only John’s baptism.
passages.en: Having heard this, they were baptized into the name of the Lord Jesus; and after Paul laid hands on them, the Holy Spirit came upon them, and they were speaking in tongues and prophesying.

passages.ctx: Paul writes to the church in Rome.
passages.en: Or are you unaware, brothers, for I speak to people who know law, that the law is master of a person for as much time as he lives?

passages.ctx: Paul sends greetings to friends in Rome.
passages.en: Greet Rufus, the chosen one in the Lord, and his mother and mine.

passages.ctx: Paul writes about spiritual gifts in worship.
passages.en: So you too, since you are eager for spirits, seek that you may abound for the building up of the church.

passages.ctx: Paul answers rivals who boast about themselves.
passages.en: Since many are boasting by the standard of the flesh, I also will boast.

passages.ctx: Paul defends his message to the Galatians.
passages.en: For am I now persuading people, or God? Or am I seeking to please people? If I were still pleasing people, I would not be Christ’s slave.

passages.ctx: Paul questions the Galatians about how they received the Spirit.
passages.en: So the one who supplies you with the Spirit and works miracles among you: is it from works of law, or from the hearing of faith?

passages.ctx: Paul worries about the Galatians.
passages.en: I am afraid for you, that I have somehow toiled over you for nothing.

passages.ctx: Paul writes to the Galatians.
passages.en: For we, by the Spirit, from faith, eagerly await the hope of righteousness.

passages.ctx: Paul writes from prison to the Ephesians.
passages.en: For this reason I ask you not to be discouraged at my afflictions for your sake, which is your glory.

passages.ctx: Paul commends Timothy to the Philippians.
passages.en: But you know his tested worth, that like a child to a father he served alongside me for the gospel.

passages.ctx: Paul writes to the church in Philippi.
passages.en: Be glad in the Lord at all times. Again I will say: be glad.

passages.ctx: Paul writes to the church in Thessalonica.
passages.en: Therefore, brothers, stand firm, and hold fast to the traditions which you were taught, whether through spoken word or through our letter.

passages.ctx: Paul gives Timothy instructions about prayer.
passages.en: So I want the men to pray in every place, raising holy hands without anger and dispute.

passages.ctx: Paul instructs Timothy about charges brought against elders.
passages.en: Do not accept an accusation against an elder unless it rests on two or three witnesses. Those who keep sinning, rebuke before everyone, so that the rest also may have fear.

passages.ctx: The writer explains how a high priest is appointed.
passages.en: And no one takes the honour upon himself; rather, he is called by God, just as Aaron too was.

passages.ctx: The writer compares Abraham with the priest Melchizedek.
passages.en: Now, with no dispute at all, the lesser one is blessed by the better one.

passages.ctx: The writer warns his readers about deliberate sin.
passages.en: For when we keep sinning by choice after receiving the full knowledge of the truth, there is no longer any sacrifice left for sins, but a certain dreadful expectation of judgment, and a zeal of fire that is about to devour the opponents.
Jesus Christ, yesterday and today, is the same, and on into the ages.

passages.ctx: James rebukes those who boast about their plans.
passages.en: But now you boast in your arrogant ways; every boast of this kind is evil. So if someone knows how to do good and does not do it, for him it is sin.

passages.ctx: Peter writes to believers who are suffering.
passages.en: So then, let those too who suffer in line with God’s will commit their souls to a faithful Creator while doing good.

passages.ctx: John writes to believers about love.
passages.en: Whoever does not love has not come to know God, since God is love.
Beloved, if this is how God loved us, we too are obliged to love one another.
Fear does not exist in love, but complete love throws fear out, because fear carries punishment, and the one who fears has not been made complete in love.
Everyone who believes that Jesus is the Christ has been born from God, and everyone who loves the father also loves the one born from him.

passages.ctx: John’s vision of the beast and its mark.
passages.en: Here is the wisdom: the one who has insight should count up the number of the beast, for it is a human being’s number, and its number is six hundred sixty-six.

passages.ctx: John’s vision of the thousand years.
passages.en: The others among the dead did not come alive until the thousand years were finished. This is the first resurrection.

notes: 2-1-2 adjective with feminine in -η (ἀγαθός, ἀγαθή, ἀγαθόν): masc./neut. like λόγος and ἔργον, fem. like ἀρχή.
Oxytone: circumflex on the ending in the genitive and dative (ἀγαθοῦ, ἀγαθῇ, ἀγαθῶν, ἀγαθοῖς).
α-contract verb: α + ε > α, α + ο/ω > ω, α + ει/ῃ > ᾳ; infinitive ἀγαπᾶν.
The stem vowel lengthens to η before tense suffixes (ἀγαπήσω, ἠγάπησα, ἠγαπήθην).
First declension feminine in -η: ἀγάπη, ἀγάπης.
Plural ἀγάπαι “love feasts” (Jude 12).
2-1-2 adjective with feminine in -η; oxytone. Verbal adjective of ἀγαπάω “love”.
Vocative ἀγαπητοί “beloved” opens many exhortations; ὁ υἱός μου ὁ ἀγαπητός “my beloved Son”.
Second declension masculine; accent moves to the penult before a long ending (ἀγγέλου, ἀγγέλων).
γγ is pronounced ng, as in English “angel”.
2-1-2 adjective with feminine in -α after ι (ἅγιος, ἁγία, ἅγιον).
Accent on the antepenult, moving to the penult before a long ending (ἁγίου, ἁγία, ἁγίων).
οἱ ἅγιοι “the saints”; τὸ πνεῦμα τὸ ἅγιον “the Holy Spirit”.
Reduplicated 2nd aorist ἤγαγον (stem ἀγαγ-); aorist passive ἤχθην.
Imperative ἄγε also means “come now!” (Jas 4:13; 5:1).
Second declension masculine; oxytone (ἀδελφοῦ, ἀδελφῷ). Vocative ἀδελφέ, plural ἀδελφοί.
The plural ἀδελφοί can include women: “brothers and sisters”, fellow believers.
Third declension neuter, stem αἱματ-: αἷμα, αἵματος.
Liquid verb: contract future ἀρῶ, aorist ἦρα (no σ); aorist infinitive ἆραι, imperative ἆρον.
Aorist passive ἤρθην.
ε-contract verb with augment αι > ῃ (ᾔτησα); middle αἰτοῦμαι is used with little difference in meaning.
Third declension, stem αἰων-: ν drops before σι (αἰῶσι); vocative = nominative.
εἰς τὸν αἰῶνα “forever”; εἰς τοὺς αἰῶνας τῶν αἰώνων “forever and ever”.
Two endings in the NT: the masculine forms serve for the feminine too (ζωὴ αἰώνιος “eternal life”).
A three-ending feminine αἰωνίαν occurs twice (2 Thess 2:16; Heb 9:12).
ε-contract verb; takes a dative object (“follow someone”).
Object in the genitive (person or sound) or accusative (thing heard).
Future ἀκούσω and middle ἀκούσομαι (same meaning); perfect ἀκήκοα (Attic reduplication).
First declension feminine with short -α after ι: genitive ἀληθείας, dative ἀληθείᾳ (the long endings pull the accent to the penult).
ἐπ’ ἀληθείας “truly”.
Strong “but, rather”, especially after a negative: οὐ … ἀλλά “not … but”.
Elided ἀλλ’ before a vowel.
Reciprocal “one another”: plural only, with no nominative.
Formed from ἄλλος doubled (ἀλλ-ηλ-); ἀγαπᾶτε ἀλλήλους “love one another”.
2-1-2 adjective with feminine in -η, but neuter singular ἄλλο without -ν (like αὐτό, τοῦτο).
οἱ ἄλλοι “the others”; ἄλλοι … ἄλλοι “some … others”.
Nasal present; 2nd aorist ἥμαρτον, future ἁμαρτήσω, perfect ἡμάρτηκα.
The NT also has a 1st aorist ἡμάρτησα: ἁμαρτήσῃ, ἁμαρτήσωμεν, ἁμαρτήσας.
First declension feminine in -α (after ι): ἁμαρτία, ἁμαρτίας. Genitive plural ἁμαρτιῶν.
Two endings: ἁμαρτωλός (masc./fem.), ἁμαρτωλόν (neut.); oxytone, so circumflex in genitive and dative.
Often a noun: “a sinner”, οἱ ἁμαρτωλοί; ἁμαρτωλός of a woman in Luke 7:37.
Hebrew “surely, truly”: closes prayers and doxologies (“amen”).
Jesus’ ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν “truly I tell you” (doubled in John: ἀμὴν ἀμήν).
A particle of contingency, usually untranslated: after relatives and conjunctions with the subjunctive it gives “-ever” (ὃς ἄν “whoever”; ὅταν = ὅτε + ἄν).
With a past indicative in an unreal condition it means “would”.
Root aorist ἀνέβην (imperative ἀνάβηθι, inf. ἀναβῆναι, ptc. ἀναβάς); future middle ἀναβήσομαι with active meaning.
NT imperatives also ἀνάβα, ἀνάβατε (Koine).
Third declension i-stem like πόλις: ἀνάστασις, ἀναστάσεως.
From ἀνίστημι “raise, rise”: ἡ ἀνάστασις τῶν νεκρῶν “the resurrection of the dead”.
Third declension with stem ἀνδρ- (δ inserted between ν and ρ): ἀνδρός, ἄνδρα, ἀνδράσι(ν); vocative ἄνερ.
An adult male or a husband; ἄνδρες ἀδελφοί “brothers!” in speeches in Acts.
Second declension masculine; accent moves from the antepenult to the penult before a long ending (ἀνθρώπου, ἀνθρώπῳ, ἀνθρώπων).
Means a human being of either sex; ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου “the Son of Man”.
Compound of ἵστημι: 1st aorist ἀνέστησα “I raised” (transitive), 2nd aorist ἀνέστην “I rose” (intransitive).
Middle ἀνίσταμαι and future middle ἀναστήσομαι are intransitive “rise”; NT imperative also ἀνάστα (for ἀνάστηθι).
The augment varies and can be double: ἤνοιξα, ἀνέῳξα, ἠνέῳξα; perfect ἀνέῳγα, ἀνέῳγμαι (NT also ἠνεῳγμένος).
Aorist passive ἠνεῴχθην, ἀνεῴχθην, ἠνοίχθην or 2nd aorist ἠνοίγην; future passive ἀνοιγήσομαι.
Liquid verb: contract future ἀπαγγελῶ, aorist ἀπήγγειλα; 2nd aorist passive ἀπηγγέλην.
Compound of ἔρχομαι: aorist ἀπῆλθον, perfect ἀπελήλυθα; deponent (middle forms, active meaning) in present and future.
NT 1st-aorist endings: ἀπῆλθαν, ἀπῆλθα.
“from, away from” (separation, origin); also cause “because of”.
Elided ἀπ’, before a rough breathing ἀφ’ (ἀφ’ οὗ “since”).
Compound of δίδωμι: ἀπέδωκα, ἀπόδος, ἀποδοῦναι; aorist middle ἀπεδόμην “sold”.
NT variants: ἀπέδετο (Heb 12:16), imperfect ἀπεδίδουν, ptc. ἀποδιδοῦν.
Present with -ισκ- suffix and iota subscript; 2nd aorist ἀπέθανον.
Future ἀποθανοῦμαι is middle (contract) with active meaning; the perfect is supplied by τέθνηκα.
Deponent: the usual aorist is passive in form with active meaning, ἀπεκρίθην “I answered” (ἀποκριθεὶς εἶπεν “he answered and said”).
Liquid stem: the rarer aorist middle ἀπεκρινάμην (ἀπεκρίνατο, 7×) has no σ.
Liquid verb: contract future ἀποκτενῶ, aorist ἀπέκτεινα; aorist passive ἀπεκτάνθην.
NT also has the present stem ἀποκτέννω (ἀποκτέννει, ἀποκτέννοντες).
-νυμι type μι-verb. Active “destroy, lose”: ἀπολέσω, ἀπώλεσα; middle “perish”: ἀπόλλυμαι, ἀπολοῦμαι, 2nd aorist ἀπωλόμην.
2nd perfect ἀπόλωλα “I am lost” (intransitive).
NT variants with thematic endings: ἀπολλύει, ἀπόλλυε; future also ἀπολῶ (1 Cor 1:19).
Compound of λύω, conjugated like it; augment after the prefix (ἀπέλυσα, ἀπελύθην).
Liquid verb: contract future ἀποστελῶ, aorist ἀπέστειλα (ε > ει, no σ).
Stem σταλ- in perfect and 2nd aorist passive (ἀπέσταλκα, ἀπέσταλμαι, ἀπεστάλην); NT perfect 3 pl also ἀπέσταλκαν.
Second declension masculine; accent moves to the penult before a long ending (ἀποστόλου, ἀποστόλων).
From ἀποστέλλω “send out”: one sent, a messenger.
Inferential “so, then, consequently”; ἄρα οὖν “so then” (Paul).
Distinguish the interrogative particle ἆρα (with circumflex).
Second declension masculine, like λόγος.
A loaf; “bread” in general; ἄρτοι τῆς προθέσεως “bread of the Presence”.
First declension feminine in -η; oxytone (ἀρχῆς, ἀρχῇ).
ἐν ἀρχῇ “in the beginning”; plural ἀρχαί “rulers, powers”.
Third declension in -ευς like βασιλεύς: ἀρχιερεύς, ἀρχιερέως.
ἀρχ- “chief” + ἱερεύς “priest”; plural οἱ ἀρχιερεῖς “the chief priests”.
Active “rule” (with genitive) is rare; the common NT use is middle ἄρχομαι “begin”, usually with an infinitive.
Aorist middle ἠρξάμην, future middle ἄρξομαι.
Deponent -άζομαι verb (middle forms, active meaning): aorist ἠσπασάμην; imperative ἀσπάσασθε “greet” in letters.
Declined like ἀγαθός, but the neuter singular is αὐτό (no -ν).
Three uses: “he, she, it, they” (mostly in the oblique cases); intensive “-self” (αὐτὸς ὁ …); “same” after the article (ὁ αὐτός).
Compound of ἵημι: κ-aorist ἀφῆκα in the indicative, root ἑ- elsewhere (ἀφῶ, ἄφες, ἀφεῖναι, ἀφείς).
Koine perfect passive ἀφέωνται (Attic ἀφεῖνται); imperfect ἤφιεν with the augment on the prefix.
NT variants with thematic endings: ἀφεῖς, ἀφίομεν, ἀφίουσι(ν); aorist 2 sg ἀφῆκες.
“until, as far as”; ἄχρι οὗ “until”.
Also spelled ἄχρις before a vowel.
Liquid verb: contract future βαλῶ, 2nd aorist ἔβαλον (NT also ἔβαλαν).
Stem βλη- in perfect and aorist passive (βέβληκα, βέβλημαι, ἐβλήθην).
-ίζω verb: ζ becomes σ before σ/θ (βαπτίσω, ἐβαπτίσθην); middle βαπτίσαι “have yourself baptized” (Acts 22:16).
First declension feminine in -α (after ι): βασιλεία, βασιλείας. Genitive plural βασιλειῶν.
Nominative plural βασιλεῖαι: circumflex because the final -αι counts as short.
Third declension in -ευς: βασιλεύς, βασιλέως, βασιλεῖ, βασιλέα; plural βασιλεῖς, βασιλέων.
Accusative plural βασιλεῖς in the NT (Attic βασιλέας). Vocative βασιλεῦ.
Labial stem: π + σ > ψ (βλέψω, ἔβλεψα); the NT uses mostly the present.
Postpositive: gives the reason or explanation — “for”.
First declension feminine in -α (after ε); oxytone, so circumflex in the genitive and dative (γενεᾶς, γενεᾷ).
α-contract verb; “beget, father” (of the father) or “bear” (of the mother); passive “be born”.
Contracted first declension (from γέα): circumflex throughout (γῆ, γῆς, γῇ, γῆν).
No plural in the NT.
Deponent: middle forms with active meaning; 2nd aorist middle ἐγενόμην (μὴ γένοιτο “may it not be”), also passive-form ἐγενήθην.
Perfect γέγονα is active in form; the pluperfect appears with and without augment (ἐγεγόνει, γεγόνει).
NT perfect 3 pl also γέγοναν.
Present with -σκ- suffix (Attic γιγνώσκω); future middle γνώσομαι with active meaning.
Root aorist ἔγνων: subj. γνῶ, imperative γνῶθι, inf. γνῶναι, ptc. γνούς.
NT variants: subjunctive γνοῖ (for γνῷ), perfect 3 pl ἔγνωκαν.
First declension feminine with short -α after σσ: genitive γλώσσης.
The circumflex becomes acute before a long ending (γλώσσης, γλώσσαις).
Third declension in -ευς like βασιλεύς: γραμματεύς, γραμματέως.
From γράμμα “letter, writing”: an expert in the Law.
First declension feminine in -η; oxytone (γραφῆς, γραφῇ).
αἱ γραφαί “the Scriptures”.
Labial stem: φ + σ > ψ (γράψω, ἔγραψα); perfect passive γέγραπται “it is written”.
2nd aorist passive ἐγράφη (no θ); perfect middle/passive 3 pl is periphrastic (γεγραμμένοι εἰσί).
Irregular: nominative γυνή, every other form from the third-declension stem γυναικ-; vocative γύναι.
Genitive and dative accent the ending (γυναικός, γυναικί, γυναικῶν); dative plural γυναιξί(ν).
Second declension neuter; accent moves to the penult before a long ending (δαιμονίου).
Postpositive (never first in its clause): “but, and, now”, marking a new step or a mild contrast.
μέν … δέ “on the one hand … on the other”; ὁ δέ “and he”. Elided δ’ before a vowel.
Impersonal (3 sg only), usually with accusative + infinitive: δεῖ με ἐλθεῖν “I must come”.
Imperfect ἔδει “it was necessary”; ptc. τὸ δέον “what is needed”, τὰ μὴ δέοντα (1 Tim 5:13).
MorphGNT files these forms under δέω; they are counted here.
2-1-2 adjective with feminine in -α after ι (δεξιός, δεξιά, δεξιόν); oxytone.
ἡ δεξιά (supply χείρ) “the right hand”; ἐκ δεξιῶν “at the right”.
2-1-2 adjective with feminine in -α after ρ (δεύτερος, δευτέρα, δεύτερον).
Ordinal “second”; ἐκ δευτέρου “a second time”.
Deponent (middle forms, active meaning); guttural stem: aorist ἐδεξάμην, perfect δέδεγμαι.
Contract verb with monosyllabic stem: aorist ἔδησα, perfect passive δέδεμαι, aorist passive ἐδέθην.
MorphGNT also files δεῖ (listed separately) and ten forms of δέομαι “ask” (ἐδεήθην, δεήθητε, δεόμενος) under δέω; they are not shown here.
NT count excludes the 10 forms of δέομαι “ask” that MorphGNT files under δέω.
+ gen. “through, by means of”; + acc. “because of, on account of”.
διὰ τοῦτο “therefore”; διὰ τί “why?”. Elided δι’ before a vowel.
Second declension masculine; accent moves to the penult before a long ending (διδασκάλου). Vocative διδάσκαλε “Teacher!”.
-σκ- present; stem διδαχ-: διδάξω, ἐδίδαξα, ἐδιδάχθην.
μι-verb with reduplicated present stem διδο-; long stem δω- in future and aorist (δώσω, ἔδωκα).
κ-aorist ἔδωκα in the indicative; other moods use the short root δο-: δῶ, δός, δοῦναι, δούς.
NT variants: subjunctive δοῖ, δώῃ, δώσῃ (for δῷ); optative δῴη (for δοίη); imperfect 3 pl ἐδίδουν.
Compound of ἔρχομαι: aorist διῆλθον, perfect διελήλυθα; deponent (middle forms, active meaning) in present, imperfect and future.
2-1-2 adjective with feminine in -α after ι (δίκαιος, δικαία, δίκαιον).
Accent moves to the penult before a long ending (δικαίου, δικαία); final -αι, -οι count as short (δίκαιαι, δίκαιοι).
First declension feminine in -η: δικαιοσύνη, δικαιοσύνης.
διά + ὅ: “therefore, for this reason”.
Guttural stem: διώξω, ἐδίωξα, ἐδιώχθην, perfect passive δεδίωγμαι.
ε-contract in the present, but aorist ἔδοξα (stem δοκ- + σ); impersonal δοκεῖ μοι “it seems to me”.
First declension feminine with short -α (not after ε, ι, ρ): genitive δόξης, dative δόξῃ.
-άζω verb: ζ becomes σ (δοξάσω, ἐδόξασα, ἐδοξάσθην); perfect passive δεδόξασμαι.
Second declension masculine; circumflex becomes acute before a long ending (δούλου, δούλων). Vocative δοῦλε.
Also an adjective “enslaved”: neuter plural δοῦλα (Rom 6:19, twice).
Deponent μι-type verb (stem δυνα-): δύναμαι, δύνασαι, δύναται; NT 2 sg also δύνῃ.
Augment ἐ- or ἠ- (ἐδύνατο, ἠδύνατο); the aorist is passive in form, ἠδυνήθην “I was able”.
Third declension i-stem like πόλις: δύναμις, δυνάμεως, δυνάμει, δύναμιν.
Plural δυνάμεις “miracles, mighty works”; also “powers” (spiritual beings).
Indeclinable except the dative δυσί(ν); same form for all genders (Attic genitive/dative δυοῖν).
οἱ δύο “the two”; ἀνὰ δύο “two by two”.
Indeclinable numeral (δύο + δέκα “two + ten”).
οἱ δώδεκα “the Twelve” (disciples).
εἰ + ἄν: “if” with the subjunctive, for a condition that may or may not be met.
After a relative it can stand for ἄν: ὃς ἐάν “whoever”.
Reflexive: no nominative; it points back to the subject (“himself, herself, itself”).
The plural also serves the first and second persons: “ourselves, yourselves, themselves”.
Contracted αὑτοῦ, αὑτῷ, αὑτόν … (rough breathing!) also occur; do not confuse with αὐτοῦ.

ego.mean: I, me; pl. ἡμεῖς we, us
notes: MorphGNT files the plural ἡμεῖς under ἐγώ, so both numbers are shown.
μου, μοι, με are enclitic; the emphatic ἐμοῦ, ἐμοί, ἐμέ are used for contrast and after most prepositions.
The nominative ἐγώ is emphatic: the verb ending already shows “I”.
Third declension neuter, stem ἐθνεσ-: σ drops between vowels and the vowels contract (ἔθνους, plural ἔθνη, ἐθνῶν).
τὰ ἔθνη “the nations, the Gentiles”.
“if”, usually with the indicative (rarely the optative); “whether” in indirect questions.
εἰ μή “except, unless”; εἰ καί “even if”. A proclitic.
Irregular μι-verb; the present indicative forms except εἶ are enclitic.
Imperfect 1 sg ἤμην and 1 pl ἤμεθα are Koine middle-type endings (Attic ἦ/ἦν, ἦμεν); 2 sg also ἦσθα.
Future ἔσομαι is middle in form (3 sg ἔσται); NT imperative 3 sg also ἤτω (1 Cor 16:22, Jas 5:12).
First declension feminine in -η: εἰρήνη, εἰρήνης.
Echoes Hebrew šālôm; a common greeting.
Motion “into, to”; goal or purpose “for” (εἰς τό + infinitive “in order to”); also “against”.
A proclitic. Do not confuse εἰς “into” with εἷς “one”.
Masculine and neuter third declension (stem ἑν-: ἑνός, ἑνί), feminine first declension (μία, μιᾶς, μιᾷ); singular only.
Distinguish εἷς “one” from the preposition εἰς and ἕν “one (neut.)” from ἐν “in”.
Can mean “a certain” or “first”: μία τῶν σαββάτων “the first day of the week”.
Compound of ἔρχομαι: aorist εἰσῆλθον, perfect εἰσελήλυθα; deponent (middle forms, active meaning) in present and future.
NT 1st-aorist endings: εἰσήλθατε, εἰσέλθατε, εἰσελθάτω.
εἰ + τε: εἴτε … εἴτε “whether … or”.
“out of, from” (source, origin, separation); also “by means of, because of”.
Before a vowel it becomes ἐξ (ἐξ αὐτοῦ, ἐξ ὕψους).
2-1-2 adjective with feminine in -η (ἕκαστος, ἑκάστη, ἕκαστον); almost always singular.
Often with a partitive genitive: ἕκαστος ὑμῶν “each of you”.
Compound of βάλλω (ἐκ > ἐξ before the augment): ἐξέβαλον, ἐκβαλῶ, ἐξεβλήθην.
“there”; ἐκεῖθεν “from there”. Related to ἐκεῖνος “that”.
Declined like αὐτός (neuter ἐκεῖνο without -ν); circumflex becomes acute before a long ending (ἐκείνου).
“That” (more remote than οὗτος), in predicate position: ἐν ἐκείναις ταῖς ἡμέραις “in those days”; alone often “he” (John).
First declension feminine in -α (after ι): ἐκκλησία, ἐκκλησίας.
Originally a citizens’ assembly; in the NT the church, local or universal.
Third declension, stem ἐλπιδ-: δ drops before σ (ἐλπίς, ἐλπίσι); vocative ἐλπί.
ἐπ’ ἐλπίδι “in hope”.
Possessive adjective of ἐγώ, declined like ἀγαθός (ἐμός, ἐμή, ἐμόν); more emphatic than μου.
The other possessives work the same way: σός “your (sg.)”, ἡμέτερος “our”, ὑμέτερος “your (pl.)”.
“in front of, before” (place, also “in the sight of”); as an adverb “ahead”.
Place “in, among”; time “in, during”; means “by, with” (ἐν μαχαίρῃ “with a sword”).
ἐν τῷ + infinitive “while, when”. A proclitic: it has no accent of its own.
First declension feminine in -η; oxytone (ἐντολῆς, ἐντολῇ).
“before, in the presence of, in the sight of”; frequent in Luke, Acts and Revelation.
An “improper” preposition: originally an adverb and never a verb prefix.
Compound of ἔρχομαι (ἐκ > ἐξ): aorist ἐξῆλθον, perfect ἐξελήλυθα; deponent (middle forms, active meaning) in present, imperfect and future.
NT 1st-aorist endings: ἐξήλθατε, ἐξῆλθαν, ἐξέλθατε.
First declension feminine in -α (after ι): ἐξουσία, ἐξουσίας.
Adverb “outside, out” (ἐξῆλθεν ἔξω “he went out”); as an improper preposition + gen. “outside of”.
οἱ ἔξω “outsiders”.
First declension feminine in -α (after ι): ἐπαγγελία, ἐπαγγελίας.
α-contract compound of ἐρωτάω; augment after the prefix: ἐπηρώτων, ἐπηρώτησα.
+ gen. “on, upon; before; in the time of”; + dat. “on, at; on the basis of”; + acc. “on, onto, to, against, over”.
Elided ἐπ’ before a smooth breathing, ἐφ’ before a rough breathing (ἐφ’ ᾧ).
Compound of γινώσκω: root aorist ἐπέγνων, future middle ἐπιγνώσομαι (active meaning), aorist passive ἐπεγνώσθην.
Indeclinable numeral: the same form for every case and gender.
Prominent in Revelation (seven churches, seals, trumpets, bowls).
Second declension neuter: nominative = accusative; plural ἔργα.
A neuter plural subject often takes a singular verb.
Two endings: ἔρημος (masc./fem.), ἔρημον (neut.).
ἡ ἔρημος (supply γῆ or χώρα) is “the wilderness, desert”; ἐν τῇ ἐρήμῳ “in the wilderness”.
Deponent in the present, imperfect and future ἐλεύσομαι (middle forms, active meaning); suppletive aorist ἦλθον and perfect ἐλήλυθα are active.
2nd aorist imperative ἐλθέ is oxytone; NT also has 1st-aorist endings: ἦλθαν, ἤλθαμεν, ἤλθατε, ἐλθάτω.
α-contract verb; NT imperfect 3 pl also ἠρώτουν (ε-contract form).
Suppletive: aorist ἔφαγον, future φάγομαι (middle in form, no σ, active meaning).
NT variants: future 2 sg φάγεσαι (Luke 17:8), subjunctive ἔσθητε (Luke 22:30, from ἔσθω).
2-1-2 adjective with feminine in -η (ἔσχατος, ἐσχάτη, ἔσχατον); accent moves to the penult before a long ending.
ἐν ταῖς ἐσχάταις ἡμέραις “in the last days”; οἱ ἔσχατοι “the last”.
2-1-2 adjective with feminine in -α after ρ (ἕτερος, ἑτέρα, ἕτερον).
Often “another, a different one”, beside ἄλλος “another (of the same kind)”, though the NT does not always keep them apart.
“still, yet; further, more”; οὐκ … ἔτι “no longer”.
Third declension neuter like ἔθνος: ἔτος, ἔτους, plural ἔτη, ἐτῶν.
Mostly middle εὐαγγελίζομαι “proclaim the good news”; the active occurs only in Rev 10:7 and 14:6.
Augment after εὐ-: εὐηγγελιζόμην, εὐηγγελισάμην.
Second declension neuter; accent moves to the penult before a long ending (εὐαγγελίου).
εὐ- “good” + ἀγγελ- “message”.
Third/first declension adjective in -υς, -εια, -υ (like βαρύς, ὀξύς): stem εὐθε- in most masc./neut. forms, fem. εὐθεῖα, εὐθείας.
The masculine εὐθύς is used as an adverb “immediately” about 50 times (above all in Mark); MorphGNT parses it as an adjective.
The adverb εὐθέως has the same meaning.

“already, now, by this time”.

Genitive plural ἡμερῶν: every first-declension noun has -ῶν. καθ’ ἡμέραν “daily”.
First declension feminine with short -α after σσ: genitive θαλάσσης, dative θαλάσσῃ.

-άζω verb: ἐθαύμασα; the aorist passive ἐθαυμάσθην also means “marveled”.

From θέλω “want, will”.
Koine form of ἐθέλω, hence the augment η- (ἤθελον, ἠθέλησα).

Regular verb like λύω; perfect passive τεθεράπευμαι (θ > τ in the reduplication).
ε-contract verb, mostly present and imperfect in the NT (“watch, observe”).
Second declension neuter, like ἔργον. In Revelation τὸ θηρίον “the beast”.

κατ’ ἰδίαν “privately”; οἱ ἴδιοι “his own people”.
“Look! See! Behold!” — calls attention to what follows; καὶ ἰδού “and behold”.

2-1-2 adjective with feminine in -α after ρ (ἱερός, ἱερά, ἱερόν).

notes: Purpose “in order that, so that”, with the subjunctive.

μι-verb with reduplicated present (ἱ- < σι-). Two aorists: 1st ἔστησα “I set” (transitive), 2nd ἔστην “I stood” (intransitive).

kago.mean: and I, I too, even I

“and I”, “I also”, “even I”. Only κἀγώ, κἀμοί, κἀμέ occur in the NT; κἀμοῦ is classical.
Deponent (middle forms, active meaning) with a perfect-like present: “I am seated”; it has no aorist (καθίζω supplies it).
Koine imperative κάθου (Attic κάθησο); NT 2 sg also κάθῃ.
Transitive “seat” or intransitive “sit down”; the augment stands before the prefix (ἐκάθισα).
“just as, as”; sometimes “since” or “how”. καθὼς γέγραπται “as it is written”.
Coordinating “and”; adverbial “also, even”.
καὶ … καί “both … and”.

“now”; ὁ νῦν αἰών “the present age”; τὰ νῦν “now, as things are”.
